newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crudes fall amid flurry of Oman deals.
newsitem.headline: Asian crudes fall amid flurry of Oman deals.

text.p: Asian crude prices were lower in outright terms on Tuesday, but most premiums were holding amid a flurry of Oman crude deals.

Traders said six cargoes may have changed hands in the last two days at premiums ranging MPM +12 to MPM +14.5 cents. Some traders were sceptical the +14.5 cents deal was done as the buyer was said to be a normally tough negotiator.
Traders said Gulf availability was drawing to a close.
In other talked deals, a U.S. major strongly denied purchasing a second Murban cargo from a French major at ADNOC +65 cents.
The major said it has purchased only one January Murban and that was at 61.5 cents per barrel from a French major.
Elsewhere, in Gulf grades a European major sold Qatar Marine to a Japanese refiner at QGPC +48 cents, prompting some confusion in the market over Qatar Marine's value.
Late last week possibly two deals were reported at premiums of 26 and 27 cents, down sharply from deals of +45 and +48.
But the latest seller said the deals in the 20s were an aberration and did not reflect the true market.
A January wet Dubai traded between a U.S. trader and a European major a full month quotes plus 80 cents, dealers said.
Paper levels were mostly steady on Tuesday with Dubai intermonth spreads reflecting a slightly firmer Dubai market, where wet premiums have risen into the 80s in recent days from low 70s.
In regional grades, the premium for in-demand Duri crude rose a notch with a major confirming it achieved ICP +65 cents in a sale of 150,000 barrels to a Japanese refiner.

Bangchak issued a January buy tender for 500,000 barrels of Gulf and 600,000 barrels of Far East light sweet grades. The tender closes on Wednesday. --Singapore, N. Fullick (+65 870 3081), Tokyo, M. Yoshikawa (+813 5473 3706)
